messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — we kicked off a canary for the new 'surge-smooth' adaptive prefetch + microbatch optimizer on a small prod slice (16 nodes) at 08:45 PT. early bench shows p50 down ~22% and token cost ~-28% on chat workloads. dashboard -> https://internal.redwood/dash/surge-smooth :tada:

deploy-bot: canary started on cluster-prod-3, nodes: gpus[gc1,gc2,gc5,gc7,...]. canary id=cs-20241002-01. config: `prefetch.adaptive=true`, `batcher.mode=microburst`

matt: huge win, congrats! any regressions on embeddings or rerank endpoints?

elaine: embeddings: p50 ~unchanged, small p99 +1-2ms on very long sequences (95th percentile seq>2048). rerank looks fine. full canary metrics in the doc: https://internal.redwood/notes/surge-smooth-canary

aria: schedule to expand to 50%? I can block out monitoring windows.

elaine: plan is to go to 30% after 12h stable, 50% on Mon 03:00 UTC if no regressions. will publish rollback window and playbook in #eng-oncall.

samir: i'll add synthetic spike tests and wire up error budget alerts to the canary id. will ping if anything crosses thresholds.

olga: love this. big kudos to infra + runtime teams :party_parrot:

ryan: can we get a short blurb for release notes / marketing? numbers + safe caveats?

elaine: yes — i'll draft. TL;DR for external: ~20-25% median latency reduction on typical chat loads, ~25-30% token cost reduction depending on request shapes; opt-in rollout, no change to API. internal doc will have perf matrix by model & seq length.

deploy-bot: canary metrics snapshot (12h): p50 -21.7%, p95 -11.9%, cost/token -26.4%, error-rate unchanged. rolling expansion to 30% now. canary id=cs-20241002-01 -> promoted:percent=30

matt: awesome. please mention any caveats around long-seq p99 slight delta in the blurb.

elaine: noted. thanks everyone — i'll post the final release note + rollout timeline in #eng-runtime and #product when we greenlight 50%.
